concepts.name: Courtyard
concepts.summary: A paved floor corner to corner with deep planting against the walls and one thing worth looking at opposite the doors. Nothing in the middle, because the middle is where you stand.

issues.message: Only 12% of the garden is under canopy, against about a third in a designed plan.

explanation.rationale: A garden built round deep planting and somewhere quiet to sit in it, organised around the terrace area. The terrace area is what this concept is not worth offering without.

decisions.text: Courtyard. No lawn fits behind the doors: a room to be in rather than a view to look at.
Chosen from 6 arrangements of this garden, on circulation, grouping and how the space is proportioned.

Designed the garden as a courtyard: a paved floor corner to corner, planting deep against the walls, and the water feature on the wall opposite the doors. Nothing stands in the middle, because the middle is where you stand.
Put the seating patio directly outside the garden doors, 6.6 × 5.1 m.
Water feature at the end of the axis, terminating the view from the doors.

concepts.name: Terrace and lawn
concepts.summary: A terrace across the doors, one clean lawn set off-centre so the planting runs deeper down one side, and the gathering places in the far corner.

issues.message: 41% of the ground has nothing designed onto it.
3 different materials, where a minimalist plan wants at most 2.

explanation.rationale: A garden built round one generous open lawn, organised around the terrace area. The terrace area is what this concept is not worth offering without.

decisions.text: Terrace and lawn. A terrace, a gap and a rear border leave 2.5 m of lawn, which reads as a strip.
Chosen from 6 arrangements of this garden, on circulation, grouping and how the space is proportioned.
Put the seating patio directly outside the garden doors, 8.0 × 3.0 m.
Water feature at the far end, on the diagonal from the doors.
